examples.text: There is scant evidence that the supplement does anything at all.
The retreating army paid scant attention to the villages it passed.
I gave scant thought to the weather and regretted it by noon.

confused.note: Scant means very little; to scan is to look over quickly.

questions.passage: The biography devotes three hundred pages to the general's battles and gives ______ attention to his later career as a teacher, which is covered in a single paragraph near the end.
questions.explanation: One paragraph out of three hundred pages is very little attention.

distractors.why: Methodical means orderly and careful, which does not fit a single paragraph.
Grave means serious, which does not describe how much attention is given.
Fleeting means lasting a short time; the sentence is about amount, not duration.

definition: done in a careful, orderly way, step by step

examples.text: A methodical search of the cave floor took the team three seasons.
The detective is methodical, checking every drawer before the obvious one.
My sister is methodical about packing and makes a list for a one-night trip.

confused.note: Methodical describes careful, orderly work; a methodology is a set of methods.

questions.passage: The auditor's approach was ______. She began with the oldest ledger, checked every entry against its receipt, and did not open the next volume until the last page of the first had been initialed.
questions.explanation: Working through each ledger in order, entry by entry, is careful and orderly.

distractors.why: Anomalous means departing from the norm, which does not fit.
Simplistic means too simple, which does not describe careful work.
Fleeting means brief, the opposite of slow, thorough checking.

definition: different from what is normal or expected

examples.text: One anomalous reading among thousands led to the discovery.
The peaceful election was anomalous in a decade of coups.
My brother's clean room was so anomalous that Mom took a photo.

confused.note: Anomalous means departing from the norm; anonymous means unnamed.

questions.passage: Every sample from the lake showed the same low level of the mineral except one. Researchers repeated the test on that ______ sample three times before concluding that the bottle had been contaminated in the laboratory.
questions.explanation: The one sample that differs from all the others departs from the norm.

distractors.why: Methodical means orderly, which does not describe a sample.
Inconclusive means not settling a question; the sample is odd, not undecided.
Grave means serious, which does not fit.

definition: treating a complicated matter as if it were much simpler than it is

examples.text: The claim that one gene causes the disease is simplistic.
It is simplistic to blame the war on a single assassination.
"Just study more" is simplistic advice for someone working two jobs.

confused.note: Simple is neutral or positive; simplistic is a criticism meaning too simple.

questions.passage: Critics called the documentary ______. It explained the famine as the result of one bad harvest and said nothing of the trade policies, land laws, and transport failures that turned a shortage into a catastrophe.
questions.explanation: Reducing a complex famine to one cause treats it as simpler than it was.

distractors.why: Counterintuitive means contrary to what one would expect, which is not the criticism.
Methodical means careful and thorough, which the film was not.
Anomalous means out of the ordinary, which does not fit.

definition: not leading to a definite result or decision

examples.text: The first trial was inconclusive, so a larger one was planned.
The battle was inconclusive; both armies claimed victory and withdrew.
The vote on pizza toppings was inconclusive, three to three.

confused.note: Inconclusive means not settling a question; inclusive means including everyone or everything.

questions.passage: After two years of testing, the results remain ______. Half the studies suggest that the treatment helps, half find no effect, and none is large enough to settle the question.
questions.explanation: Studies split evenly with none decisive do not settle the matter.

distractors.why: Counterintuitive means surprising; the problem is that the results decide nothing.
Scant means very little, but there are many studies.
Grave means serious, which does not fit.

examples.text: The contamination necessitated a second round of tests.
The loss of the fleet necessitated a treaty.
A flat tire necessitated a long walk home.

confused.note: Necessitate is the verb; a necessity is something needed.

questions.passage: The discovery of a crack in the main support ______ the closing of the bridge. Engineers said it could not safely carry traffic until the beam had been replaced.
questions.explanation: The crack made closing the bridge necessary.

distractors.why: Commended means praised, which does not fit.
Hypothesized means proposed as an explanation, which does not fit.
Weathered means came safely through, which does not fit.

definition: to come safely through a difficult period or experience

examples.text: The small republic weathered three invasions in a century.
Lichens can weather years of drought and revive within hours of rain.
Our friendship weathered a whole summer of living in the same tent.

confused.note: To weather is to come through hardship; whether introduces a choice.

questions.passage: Many small shops closed during the recession. The bakery ______ the crisis, however, by cutting its hours, baking fewer kinds of bread, and delivering to customers who could no longer afford to drive.
questions.explanation: Staying open through the recession is coming safely through a hard time.

distractors.why: Necessitated means made necessary, which does not fit.
Expounded means explained in detail, which does not fit.
Commended means praised, which does not fit.

examples.text: The loss of the grain fleet placed the city in grave danger.
Doctors expressed grave concern about the spread of the infection.
Forgetting my mom's birthday was a grave mistake.

confused.note: Grave means very serious; gravel is small stones.

questions.passage: The engineer's report used unusually strong language. It warned that the dam posed a ______ risk to the towns below and urged that they be evacuated before the next heavy rain.
questions.explanation: A risk that calls for evacuation is very serious.

distractors.why: Scant means very slight, the opposite of a risk that requires evacuation.
Fleeting means brief, which does not convey seriousness.
Simplistic means oversimplified, which does not fit.

definition: lasting for only a very short time

examples.text: The particle's existence is fleeting, a fraction of a billionth of a second.
She catches a fleeting glimpse of the sea between two hills.
I had a fleeting urge to clean my room, and then it passed.

confused.note: Fleeting means very brief; floating means resting on a liquid.

questions.passage: The rare bird appeared at the edge of the clearing for only a few seconds. The ______ sighting was enough, however, for one photographer to capture the first image of the species in forty years.
questions.explanation: A sighting of a few seconds lasts a very short time.

distractors.why: Methodical means orderly and careful, which does not describe a brief glimpse.
Inconclusive means not decisive, but the photograph was a clear success.
Grave means serious, which does not fit.

definition: to praise someone or something, especially formally

examples.text: The queen commended the sailors for their courage in the storm.
Reviewers commended the study for the care of its design.
The principal commended our class for cleaning the park.

confused.note: To commend is to praise; to command is to order.

questions.passage: At the ceremony, the mayor ______ the firefighters who had rescued eleven people from the burning hotel. Each received a medal and a letter of thanks signed by every member of the council.
questions.explanation: Medals and letters of thanks are formal praise.

distractors.why: Necessitated means made necessary, which does not fit.
Weathered means came through a difficulty, which does not fit.
Hypothesized means proposed as an explanation, which does not fit.

definition: the opposite of what you would expect to be true

examples.text: It is counterintuitive, but adding a road can make traffic slower.
The general's counterintuitive decision to retreat won him the war.
It seems counterintuitive that a nap can make you more tired.

confused.note: Counterintuitive means contrary to expectation; counteractive means working against something.

questions.passage: The finding is ______. One would expect that giving customers more choices would raise sales, yet shops that offered six kinds of jam sold ten times as much as those that offered twenty-four.
questions.explanation: A result opposite to what one would expect goes against intuition.

distractors.why: Inconclusive means not settling a question, but this result is clear.
Simplistic means oversimplified, which is not what the sentence says.
Methodical means orderly, which does not describe a surprising result.

partsNote: against what one sees at once

definition: to suggest an explanation for something that has not yet been proved

examples.text: Researchers hypothesize that the birds navigate by the stars.
Scholars hypothesize that the city was abandoned after a drought.
I hypothesize that the dog, not my brother, ate the leftovers.

confused.note: To hypothesize is to propose an explanation; to hypnotize is to put into a trance.

questions.passage: No one knows why the whales sing. Some biologists ______ that the songs attract mates; others suspect that they help the animals keep track of one another across great distances.
questions.explanation: Proposing unproved explanations for the songs is hypothesizing.

distractors.why: Commend means to praise, which does not fit.
Necessitate means to make necessary, which does not fit.
Weather means to come through hardship, which does not fit.

definition: to explain something by talking or writing about it in detail

examples.text: The envoy expounded his king's position for two hours.
The professor expounds on the meaning of a comma while his soup grows cold.
My uncle will expound on the proper way to grill corn if you let him.

confused.note: To expound is to explain in detail; to expand is to grow larger.

questions.passage: Asked a simple question about the origin of the town's name, the guide ______ on the subject for nearly an hour, covering three languages, two legends, and a medieval tax record.
questions.explanation: Speaking in detail for an hour is explaining at length.

distractors.why: Hypothesized means proposed an unproved explanation, which does not capture speaking at length.
Commended means praised, which does not fit.
Weathered means came through a difficulty, which does not fit.
